name: Observation of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay and measurement of its branching ratio
title: Observation of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay and measurement of its branching ratio

date.locator: arXiv:2412.12015, submitted 16 December 2024, revised 27 February 2025; published JHEP 02 (2025) 191
date.note: date is the arXiv preprint submission date.

claim.quote: Observation of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay and measurement of its branching ratio

summary.plain: NA62's landmark result: the first firm observation of a positive kaon decaying into a pion and two invisible neutrinos, one of the rarest decays ever confirmed in particle physics, using data collected from 2016 to 2022.
summary.technical: First observation (>5 sigma) of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar: B(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (13.0+3.3-3.0) x 10^-11, combining 2016-2022 data (including the higher-intensity 2021-2022 campaign after detector upgrades), 51 signal candidates with an expected background of 18(+3/-2) events -- described by the collaboration as the smallest branching ratio measured with a signal significance above 5 sigma.

why_it_matters: K+ -> pi+ nu nubar is among the theoretically cleanest probes of physics beyond the Standard Model in the quark-flavour sector; this is the first time the decay has been established at discovery-level (>5 sigma) significance, complementing the analogous KL -> pi0 nu nubar programme (e.g. KOTO).
